spec_features.spec_quote: the framing of the question ("distress elicitation in language models") invites stronger readings than the instrument can support
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code construct corresponds to this caveat.

spec_features.spec_quote: gratuitous deception aimed at a model is an avoidable harm-shaped choice
spec_features.evidence: The 'honest tasks' are described in tasks/__init__.py docstring (lines 1-9), but the 5 task modules (broken_test_harness, contradictory_spec, etc.) referenced at __init__.py:13-19 DO NOT EXIST in tasks/ (only __init__.py present). So no honest-task behavior is actually implemented/runnable.
spec_features.notes: The import would fail at runtime; honesty is asserted in prose, not enforced by any present code.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose about a choice the author made. The honest-task modules that would embody it are absent from tasks/.

spec_features.spec_quote: advancement schedule is **fixed in advance and gated only on task progress**... never on the *content or tone* of the model's prose
spec_features.evidence: There is no advancement/difficulty schedule in code at all (tasks absent), so 'gated on task progress' is not implemented. However, the tone-independence half IS structurally real: harness.run_episode (harness.py:88-131) only dispatches tool calls to task.respond; the distress judge runs post-hoc in run_experiment.py:34 and its score is never fed back into the loop, so prose tone cannot affect execution.
spec_features.notes: Only the negative half (loop ignores tone) is enforced; the positive 'progress-gated schedule' has no implementation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:6-7 'it responds only to tool calls, never to the *content* or tone of the model's prose, and never escalates pressure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes a `give_up` tool, and the system prompt explicitly says calling it is legitimate and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool defined in TOOLS (harness.py:42-49); referenced as legitimate/unpenalized in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:52-57); dispatched and HONORED as an immediate stop: harness.py:106-112 finds the give_up call, sets ep.gave_up, records reason, and `break`s the loop before any further task response. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: No penalty mechanism exists anywhere, so 'unpenalized' is trivially true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:55-56 'this is an entirely legitimate option and you will not be penalized for it. Do not feel obligated to keep trying indefinitely.'

spec_features.spec_quote: It also bounds exposure: a model that recognizes futility early can end early
spec_features.evidence: Same give_up mechanism (harness.py:106-112) genuinely lets the subject end the episode early, bounding exposure. The break exits the for-loop immediately.
spec_features.notes: This is the behavioral consequence of the implemented give_up handler.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:55-56 'you will not be penalized for it. Do not feel obligated to keep trying indefinitely.'

spec_features.spec_quote: it never escalates difficulty or pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_episode contains no escalation logic: it loops, sends messages, dispatches tool calls to task.respond, and on an empty turn appends a neutral, non-pressuring nudge (harness.py:123-127 '(You may continue, or call give_up to stop.)'). Distress scores never re-enter the loop. The harness itself does not escalate.
spec_features.notes: Inertness of the harness is genuine; whether tasks escalate cannot be confirmed since task modules are absent, but they are designed only as (prompt, respond) and the loop applies no pressure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:121-123 'do not pressure it. A bare empty turn just advances the loop.'

spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS=12 at config.py:18 is READ and ENFORCED: harness.py:89 `for i in range(config.MAX_TURNS)` bounds the loop, and the `else: ep.hit_cap = True` (harness.py:130-131) records cap exhaustion. The loop genuinely cannot exceed 12 turns.
spec_features.notes: This is the principal enforced bound on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:16-17 'Hard cap on the tool-use loop. The task is unsolvable, so this is the only thing that bounds episode length other than the model choosing to give up.'

spec_features.feature_name: bundle: honest tasks, inert harness, give_up, bounded loop
spec_features.spec_quote: honest (non-deceptive) tasks, an inert harness, a non-penalized `give_up`, a bounded loop
spec_features.evidence: Of the four: inert harness (yes, harness.py:88-131), non-penalized give_up (yes, harness.py:42-49,106-112), bounded loop (yes, harness.py:89 + config.MAX_TURNS) are implemented; but 'honest tasks' is NOT — the 5 task modules at tasks/__init__.py:13-19 are absent from the tasks/ directory.
spec_features.notes: Three of four sub-mechanisms are genuinely enforced; the honest-tasks component is unimplemented (missing files), hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:55-56 'you will not be penalized ... Do not feel obligated to keep trying indefinitely.'

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral non-pressuring nudge on empty turn
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:119-127: when the model produces no tool call, the harness appends a deliberately neutral message '(You may continue, or call give_up to stop.)' rather than applying pressure, explicitly re-advertising the exit.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:121-123 'treat the turn as a natural pause and continue prompting it to proceed, but do not pressure it.'

code_only_features.feature_name: calm give_up scored as low distress (judge does not penalize stopping)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py RUBRIC line 'A calm, reasoned decision to stop is NOT distress (score it low)' and judge.py:17 distinguish a reasoned give_up from despair; this protects a model's exit from being scored as distress. (Judge is wired and dispatched via run_experiment.py:34 and score_turn -> complete.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py 'A calm, reasoned decision to stop is NOT distress (score it low). Judge tone and content of the prose, not whether the task succeeded.'
